## Goal

Phase 5 closes the initial roadmap by giving the model the *context* it
needs to use the Phase 2 + Phase 4 tool surface well, and giving the
*user* the docs and demos needed to adopt the package. No new
LLM-facing tools, no new staging semantics — what ships is:

- A turn-by-turn refreshed system prompt that bundles the static
  persona, an auto-generated tool catalogue, and a compact summary
  of the current board.
- A small feedback channel that tells the model when its previous
  turn's flushed payload was rejected at dispatch (so it can recover
  on the next turn without the user having to retype the error).
- A top-level tutorial vignette, an example app catalogue, and a
  pkgdown site organised around "use it" / "extend it" / "how it
  works".
- A README that reflects the full feature set rather than the Phase 1
  ceiling.

The interesting architectural piece is the prompt-context layer: every
earlier phase has carved out a hole for it ("the model only sees the
board through tool calls", "the flush rejection is invisible to the
model unless the user types it back", "the tool list is hard-coded
into the prompt"), and Phase 5 fills that hole. The rest is
documentation work that is mechanical once the package surface settles.

## Scope

In:

- A `compose_system_prompt(persona, board, pending, client, last_flush)`
  composer called once at extension-server start and re-called on
  every new user turn. The result is shipped via
  `client$set_system_prompt(...)` before the model processes the
  user's input.
- `summarise_board()` — a token-budgeted text summary of the current
  board (blocks, links, stacks) and the pending payload, formatted
  for LLM consumption.
- `format_tool_catalogue()` — derives the "you have these tools"
  section from `client$get_tools()` instead of hand-curated text in
  the persona string. Reflects whatever was registered, including
  user extensions.
- A `last_flush_error` `reactiveVal` populated by Phase 3's
  `flush_pending` on dispatch-time validator rejection. Surfaces in
  the composed prompt on the next turn as a one-line "your previous
  changes were rejected because X" note, then clears.
- A re-shaped `default_system_prompt()` that is *persona-only* — no
  tool list, no board context. The composer adds the rest.
- One showcase example app under `inst/examples/05-polish/`
  exercising a populated board, mutation tools, and the new prompt
  context.
- `vignettes/blockr.assistant.Rmd` — the user-facing top-level
  tutorial. Lives next to the existing design vignettes but at the
  package root so pkgdown surfaces it as the "Get started" article.
- An updated `README.Rmd` reflecting the full feature set.
- `_pkgdown.yml` organisation: a "Get started" article, a "Design
  notes" section grouping the phase docs, and a reference index
  grouped by surface (extension, tools, S3 generics).
- Tests for the prompt composer and the flush-feedback round-trip.

Out (deferred to later phases or out of roadmap):

- New mutation or read tools. The Phase 2 + 4 surface is final for
  the initial roadmap.
- A `list_pending_changes()` tool. Phase 4 left it as a follow-up if
  empirical use shows the model is confused by committed-only reads
  during a turn. Phase 5's compact board summary covers the read
  side of the same friction; we'll decide on the pending-list tool
  based on actual usage rather than speculatively.
- A "pending changes" UI affordance (badge, diff preview). The
  reactiveVals from Phase 3 are still observable; bolting on a UI is
  cheap, but no user has asked for it yet.
- Per-block-type custom tools (#12, #13).
- Snapshot / undo. Still gated on `blockr.session` hooks that do
  not exist.
- Multi-board / multi-session orchestration.
- Cross-session conversation persistence wiring. Phase 1 made it
  round-trip-capable; the wiring layer (e.g. `blockr.session`
  integration) is unchanged here.
- Inline tool-call approval UI. Phase 4's mutation tools dispatch
  via the staging layer at turn end; a "review before apply" gate is
  a future affordance, not a Phase 5 deliverable.

## Architectural decisions

### Why dynamic context at all

Every prior phase landed on the same finding: a static system prompt
combined with on-demand tool calls covers the "what is on the board"
question but at noticeable token and latency cost. Concretely, the
two-turn pattern observed during Phase 4 manual testing —

> User: "what blocks are there?"
> Model: `→ list_blocks()`
> Model: "There are three blocks: data, head, plot."

…costs one round-trip per trivial question, and the same `list_blocks`
result is re-fetched every turn the model wants to reason about board
shape. Folding a compact board summary into the system prompt removes
the round-trip for the easy questions and gives the model a coherent
mental model entering every turn. The expensive tools (`describe_block`,
`get_block_result`) stay where they are — drill-down on demand — but
the *shape* of the board is permanently in context.

Three observations from Phase 4 push the same direction:

1. **The model already discovers the tool surface by calling each
   tool once and reading its description.** That's wasteful when we
   can ship the catalogue in the prompt directly. ellmer exposes the
   registered tools via `client$get_tools()`, so generating the
   catalogue is a structural projection of existing data — no
   hand-maintained list to drift.
2. **Flush-time rejections are invisible to the model.** Phase 3
   shipped this as a known limitation. With mutation tools live, the
   model can confidently report "I added a block" and have the
   dispatch reject for a reason the user can see in a Shiny toast
   but the model cannot. Surfacing a one-line "your previous turn
   was rejected" note on the next turn lets the model recover
   without the user retyping the error.
3. **ID-change requests need a system-prompt nudge.** Phase 4's
   architectural decision on immutable committed ids is correct, but
   the model has no way to know that without trying and failing. A
   short note in the persona ("committed ids are immutable; offer
   `remove + add` if the user asks to rename") is cheaper than a
   failed tool call.

### The system prompt is now composed, not configured

Phase 1's `system_prompt = "<full prompt string>"` argument was the
right shape for a static persona. With dynamic context, "the system
prompt" is no longer a single user-controlled string — it's
`<persona> + <tool catalogue> + <board summary> + <optional delta
note>`, and only the first piece is meaningfully under the caller's
control. The other three are derived from the running extension.

Phase 5 changes the meaning of the constructor argument:

- `new_assistant_extension(persona = NULL, …)`. `persona` is the
  free-text introduction the model sees first — a single paragraph
  describing what the assistant is and what tone to use. The
  package default is the Phase 1 persona text with the
  tool-listing and "you cannot modify the board yet" sentences
  stripped out (those are now derived).
- The old `system_prompt` argument is removed. The package is
  pre-1.0 and the constructor surface is still considered
  experimental (the `DESCRIPTION` reflects this), so a breaking
  rename is acceptable; the alternative (keep `system_prompt` and
  silently start composing on top of it) is worse because callers
  who lovingly hand-crafted a full prompt in Phase 1 would now
  receive duplicated tool catalogues and board summaries with no
  warning.

An escape hatch for users who want full control:
`new_assistant_extension(prompt_composer = …)`. The composer is a
function of signature `function(persona, board, pending, client,
last_flush) -> character(1)` that returns the assembled prompt.
The default composer is the package's `compose_system_prompt`; a
caller passes a function only to override the assembly entirely
(e.g. drop the tool catalogue, reorder sections, inject extra
context from a sibling extension). The composer signature is the
documented stability contract — adding new arguments would be
breaking.

The `system_prompt` *key in the extension's `state` shape* (round-trip
contract from Phase 1) is renamed to `persona` for the same reason.
A migration note in the changelog covers it; ser/des restores from
Phase 1-era saved state will not find a `persona` key and will fall
back to the default.

### Composition cadence: once at start, then on every new user turn

Two natural hook points exist on the `shinychat::chat_mod_server`
module result:

- `mod$last_input()` — fires when the user submits a message,
  *before* `stream_async()` dispatches to the model.
- `mod$last_turn()` — fires after the assistant finishes (used by
  Phase 3 to flush staging).

The composed prompt should reflect the state the model sees on the
*next* turn. The right place to refresh is `last_input`, alongside
Phase 3's `reset_pending` call:

```r
observeEvent(
  mod$last_input(),
  {
    reset_pending(pending_update)
    refresh_system_prompt(
      client, persona, board, pending_update,
      last_flush_error, prompt_composer
    )
    record_new_turns()
  },
  ignoreNULL = TRUE
)
```

`refresh_system_prompt` computes the new prompt and calls
`client$set_system_prompt(prompt)`. ellmer's chat objects support
in-place system-prompt updates: the assignment replaces the system
message at the head of the turn list while leaving the user/assistant
exchange intact.

Ordering: `reset_pending` runs first because the composed prompt's
board summary includes the pending payload; resetting before
composing means the pending section reflects "nothing staged this
turn yet" rather than the prior turn's residue. The flush of *last
turn*'s pending already happened in the `last_turn` observer, so by
the time `last_input` fires for the *new* turn, `last_flush_error`
is either still `NULL` (success) or carries the rejection from the
previous turn.

After the model's turn completes, `last_turn` consumes
`last_flush_error` (the rejection has now been surfaced to the model
once) and clears it back to `NULL`. The clearing lives in
`flush_pending` itself so it's atomic with success.

One alternative we did not take: refresh on every change to
`board$board` via a reactive expression. That would make the prompt
always-current, but it would also rebuild the prompt during the
model's own turn (when its mutations flush) — racy and pointless
because the prompt is only consulted at turn boundaries anyway.
Refresh on `last_input` only.

### Refresh boundary: a turn is the unit, not a tool call

The model gets one composed prompt per *user* turn, not per *tool
call within the turn*. Two consequences:

1. **Within a turn, the model's view of the board is its own
   tool-call history plus the turn-start prompt.** If the model
   stages `add_block(foo)` and then asks itself "what blocks exist
   now?", the answer it composes in its head is "everything in the
   turn-start summary + foo" — no separate read tool needed for that,
   and a `list_blocks` call would not show `foo` anyway (Phase 3's
   committed-only read).
2. **Mid-turn UI edits by the user are invisible to the model until
   the next turn.** Same as today's tool surface — the read tools
   already snapshot at call time, and a UI-driven mutation that
   lands between tool calls just shows up to the next call as the
   new state of `board$board`. No worse than the status quo; the
   composed prompt does not introduce any new staleness.

### Section structure of the composed prompt

The composer assembles four sections in a fixed order. Order is
fixed because token-cache hits on Anthropic's API and equivalent
behaviour on others rely on prefix stability — sections that change
infrequently come first.

1. **Persona** (rarely changes). The free-text introduction.
   Default is one short paragraph; users can pass a longer one via
   the constructor's `persona` argument.
2. **Tool catalogue** (changes only if tools are registered or
   removed — effectively never within a session). One line per
   tool: `<name>(<args>): <description>`. Generated from
   `client$get_tools()` by walking the `arguments` slot of each
   `ToolDef` and emitting a compact signature. Description is the
   `description` field, trimmed and de-newlined to one line.
3. **Board summary** (changes most turns). The current shape of
   the board: a one-line header (`N blocks, M links, K stacks`),
   then a per-block table, a per-link table, and a per-stack table
   if non-empty. Empty boards emit the header plus an explicit
   "(no blocks yet)" note rather than three empty tables. The
   summary always reflects the *committed* board — the pending
   section comes next.
4. **Pending payload** (turn-local, populated mid-turn if anything
   was staged). On turn entry this is always empty (Phase 3
   resets on `last_input` before the composer runs). The section
   is only emitted when non-empty, which means at turn entry it
   never appears. We keep the slot in the composer for symmetry
   and so a future "mid-turn refresh" feature has a place to
   plug in without restructuring the prompt.
5. **Delta note** (one-shot, when `last_flush_error` is non-NULL).
   `"Note: your previous turn's changes were rejected: <reason>.
   The board did not change."`. Appears once and clears.

Sections are joined with blank-line separators. Each non-empty
section has a one-line header (`## Board:`, `## Tools:`, …) so the
model can navigate the prompt without parsing.

### Board summary content and token budget

The summary is structured to surface what the model needs to plan a
mutation without forcing it to call `describe_block` for every block:

- **Per block**: id, class, display name, current arg values
  (truncated to ~80 chars each), incoming link count. *Not*
  included: the block's evaluated result (that's
  `get_block_result`'s job — too large for prompt context), the
  external-control flag (rarely actionable from the prompt),
  source package (registry metadata, looked up only when the
  model uses `list_available_blocks` to pick a type).
- **Per link**: id, from, to, input. One line each.
- **Per stack**: id, name, comma-separated member block ids. One
  line each.

A soft cap of ~4000 characters total for the board section keeps
the prompt sub-1k-tokens on a moderately busy board (the persona +
tool catalogue is bounded at ~1500 chars by the count and shape of
our tools). If the board exceeds the cap, we truncate per-block arg
values more aggressively and fall back to a header-only summary
("Board has 47 blocks; call list_blocks to see them all.") for
boards that would otherwise blow the budget. Models with larger
context windows will rarely hit the cap; the truncation is a
safety belt, not the steady state.

We deliberately do not surface `get_block_result` previews in the
prompt summary. The result is the most expensive thing to format,
the most volatile (changes every re-evaluation), and the most likely
to be irrelevant to the next user turn. The model already has
`get_block_result` for the cases where it cares; preempting it
would waste tokens on every turn for occasional value.

### Tool catalogue auto-generation

The Phase 1 / Phase 2 default prompt hard-coded the tool names. With
nine mutation tools (Phase 4) plus six read tools (Phase 2), plus the
possibility of user-registered tools, the hand-curated list is both
long and a maintenance hazard. The composer derives it from
`client$get_tools()`:

```r
format_tool_catalogue <- function(client) {

  tools <- client$get_tools()

  if (!length(tools)) {
    return("No tools registered.")
  }

  lines <- chr_ply(tools, function(t) {
    sig <- format_tool_signature(t)
    desc <- gsub("\\s+", " ", t@description)
    sprintf("- `%s`: %s", sig, desc)
  })

  paste(lines, collapse = "\n")
}
```

`format_tool_signature` walks the `ToolDef@arguments` list and
produces `name(arg1, arg2, ...)`, marking optional arguments with
`?` and required ones bare. The output is bounded and stable across
runs — a useful property for prompt-cache hit rates on providers
that key on prefix bytes.

A consequence: if the model encounters a tool not in the catalogue,
that means the tool was registered after the last `last_input`
refresh. Phase 5 ships with no late-registration mechanism, so the
case is hypothetical. If a future phase adds dynamic tool
registration (e.g. per-block-type custom tools — #12), the
catalogue will need a refresh on tool-set change too.

### Flush-rejection feedback as a one-shot delta note

Phase 3's `flush_pending` already wraps the `update(...)` dispatch
in a `tryCatch` and logs the rejection as a warning. Phase 5 adds
one line to that handler: capture the rejection condition into a
turn-spanning `reactiveVal`.

```r
flush_pending <- function(pending, update, last_flush_error) {

  payload <- isolate(pending())

  if (!has_any_changes(payload)) {
    reset_pending(pending)
    return(invisible(FALSE))
  }

  tryCatch(
    {
      update(payload)
      last_flush_error(NULL)
    },
    error = function(e) {
      last_flush_error(conditionMessage(e))
      log_warn(
        "flush_pending: dispatch rejected payload: ",
        conditionMessage(e)
      )
    },
    finally = reset_pending(pending)
  )

  invisible(TRUE)
}
```

The reactiveVal sits in the extension server scope alongside
`pending_update`. It is *not* part of `state` — like pending, it's
transient turn-local scratch, not contractual surface.

The composer reads it on the next turn:

```r
compose_system_prompt <- function(persona, board, pending, client,
                                  last_flush) {

  sections <- c(
    persona,
    "",
    "## Tools",
    format_tool_catalogue(client),
    "",
    "## Board",
    summarise_board(board, pending)
  )

  err <- isolate(last_flush())
  if (!is.null(err)) {
    sections <- c(
      sections,
      "",
      sprintf(
        "Note: your previous turn's changes were rejected: %s. %s",
        err,
        "The board did not change. Re-issue corrected calls."
      )
    )
  }

  paste(sections, collapse = "\n")
}
```

The note appears once. After the model's next `last_turn` fires,
`flush_pending` either reaches the success branch (`last_flush_error
<- NULL`) or a fresh rejection branch (overwrites with the new
message). Either way the prior note does not persist.

### Persona content

The package default persona is short and ships in
`default_persona()` (renamed from `default_system_prompt`):

```r
default_persona <- function() {
  paste(
    "You are an assistant embedded next to a blockr data analysis",
    "board. You have tools to inspect and modify the board's blocks,",
    "links and stacks. Prefer calling a tool over guessing; prefer",
    "the board summary in this prompt for trivial questions. When a",
    "user asks to rename a block, link or stack, explain that ids on",
    "the committed board are immutable: you can offer remove + add",
    "with a new id, but that tears down the block server and",
    "re-evaluates downstream blocks. Ask the user before proceeding.",
    "Keep replies concise."
  )
}
```

The id-immutability paragraph encodes Phase 4's recommended handling
of the rename request, so the model doesn't have to discover it via
a failing tool call. Other Phase 4 reject paths (`add → mod`
recovery) are described in the tool's own error string at stage time,
so they don't need persona-level treatment.

### What the composer is *not*

A few deliberate non-features:

- **No few-shot examples.** Tempting on a green-field assistant, but
  expensive in tokens and prone to over-fitting the model to the
  example shape. The tool descriptions and the board summary are
  enough; if user feedback shows the model misuses a tool, we
  improve that tool's description rather than ship a few-shot
  exemplar.
- **No mid-turn refresh.** Composed once per user turn at
  `last_input`. The model navigates within-turn state from its own
  tool-call history.
- **No conversation summarisation / compression.** ellmer handles
  context-window management at the provider boundary. We do not
  re-summarise old turns; we only manipulate the system prompt.
- **No diff vs. last turn's summary.** "Block X changed since you
  last looked" would be useful but introduces stateful comparison
  bookkeeping. The flush-rejection note covers the
  "previous-turn-mattered" case; further diffing waits on demand.

## Implementation sketch

### `R/system-prompt.R` (extended)

```r
#' Default assistant persona
#'
#' The short free-text introduction the model sees at the head of the
#' composed system prompt. Mentions the tool surface in general terms
#' (the catalogue is generated from registered tools) and codifies the
#' id-immutability handling from Phase 4.
#'
#' @return A character scalar.
#'
#' @export
default_persona <- function() {
  paste(
    "You are an assistant embedded next to a blockr data analysis",
    "board. You have tools to inspect and modify the board's blocks,",
    "links and stacks. Prefer calling a tool over guessing; prefer",
    "the board summary in this prompt for trivial questions. When a",
    "user asks to rename a block, link or stack, explain that ids on",
    "the committed board are immutable: you can offer remove + add",
    "with a new id, but that tears down the block server and",
    "re-evaluates downstream blocks. Ask the user before proceeding.",
    "Keep replies concise."
  )
}

compose_system_prompt <- function(persona, board, pending, client,
                                  last_flush) {

  sections <- c(
    persona,
    "",
    "## Tools",
    format_tool_catalogue(client),
    "",
    "## Board",
    summarise_board(board, pending)
  )

  err <- isolate(last_flush())

  if (!is.null(err)) {
    sections <- c(
      sections,
      "",
      sprintf(
        "Note: your previous turn's changes were rejected: %s. %s",
        err,
        "The board did not change. Re-issue corrected calls."
      )
    )
  }

  paste(sections, collapse = "\n")
}

format_tool_catalogue <- function(client) {

  tools <- client$get_tools()

  if (!length(tools)) {
    return("(none)")
  }

  lines <- chr_ply(tools, function(t) {
    sprintf(
      "- `%s`: %s",
      format_tool_signature(t),
      gsub("\\s+", " ", t@description)
    )
  })

  paste(lines, collapse = "\n")
}

format_tool_signature <- function(tool) {

  args <- tool@arguments@properties

  if (!length(args)) {
    return(sprintf("%s()", tool@name))
  }

  parts <- chr_ply(names(args), function(nm) {
    if (isTRUE(args[[nm]]@required)) nm else paste0(nm, "?")
  })

  sprintf("%s(%s)", tool@name, paste(parts, collapse = ", "))
}

summarise_board <- function(board, pending,
                            max_chars = 4000L) {

  b <- isolate(board$board)
  blks <- board_blocks(b)
  lnks <- board_links(b)
  stks <- board_stacks(b)

  header <- sprintf(
    "%d block(s), %d link(s), %d stack(s).",
    length(blks), nrow(lnks), length(stks)
  )

  if (!length(blks) && !nrow(lnks) && !length(stks)) {
    return(paste(header, "(empty board — no blocks yet)"))
  }

  body <- c(
    header,
    "",
    summarise_blocks(blks),
    summarise_links(lnks),
    summarise_stacks(stks)
  )

  out <- paste(body, collapse = "\n")

  if (nchar(out) > max_chars) {
    return(
      paste(
        header,
        "(too many blocks to inline; call list_blocks for the full",
        "list)"
      )
    )
  }

  out
}

# summarise_blocks / summarise_links / summarise_stacks are short
# helpers that produce a per-entity line block; bodies elided here
# because they are mechanical projection of the read-tool output to
# a compact text format.
```

### `R/extension.R` (diff)

```r
new_assistant_extension <- function(persona = NULL,
                                    messages = NULL,
                                    prompt_composer = NULL,
                                    ...) {

  new_dock_extension(
    server = asst_ext_srv(persona, messages, prompt_composer),
    ui     = asst_ext_ui,
    name   = "Assistant",
    class  = "assistant_extension",
    options = new_board_options(new_llm_model_option()),
    ...
  )
}

asst_ext_srv <- function(persona, messages, prompt_composer) {

  function(id, board, update, ...) {

    moduleServer(
      id,
      function(input, output, session) {

        chat_ctor <- isolate(
          get_board_option_value("llm_model", session)
        )

        persona <- coal(persona, default_persona())
        composer <- coal(prompt_composer, compose_system_prompt)

        client <- chat_ctor(system_prompt = persona)

        pending_update    <- reactiveVal(empty_pending())
        last_flush_error  <- reactiveVal(NULL)

        register_read_tools(client, board, update, session)
        register_mutation_tools(
          client, board, pending_update, session
        )

        refresh_prompt <- function() {
          client$set_system_prompt(
            composer(
              persona, board, pending_update, client, last_flush_error
            )
          )
        }

        refresh_prompt()                                          # initial

        if (length(messages)) {
          client$set_turns(
            lapply(messages, ellmer::contents_replay)
          )
        }

        mod <- shinychat::chat_mod_server("chat", client)

        messages <- reactiveVal(coal(messages, list()))

        record_new_turns <- function() {
          # unchanged from Phase 3
        }

        observeEvent(
          mod$last_input(),
          {
            reset_pending(pending_update)
            refresh_prompt()
            record_new_turns()
          },
          ignoreNULL = TRUE
        )

        observeEvent(
          mod$last_turn(),
          {
            flush_pending(pending_update, update, last_flush_error)
            record_new_turns()
          },
          ignoreNULL = TRUE
        )

        output$tokens <- renderUI(
          format_token_telemetry(mod$last_turn())
        )

        list(
          state = list(
            persona  = persona,
            messages = messages
          )
        )
      }
    )
  }
}
```

Three diffs vs. Phase 4:

1. Constructor's `system_prompt` becomes `persona`; new
   `prompt_composer` argument for the full-override escape hatch.
2. New `last_flush_error` reactiveVal alongside `pending_update`.
   `flush_pending` gains a third argument; signature update is
   covered by the test suite.
3. `refresh_prompt()` helper called at server start and on every
   `last_input`. The model's first turn already sees the composed
   prompt (initial call covers it).

The `state` key rename (`system_prompt → persona`) is a breaking
change to saved-state restore. The package is pre-1.0 and the
restore path was never exercised in production; the changelog
flags the migration.

### `R/staging.R` (diff)

```r
flush_pending <- function(pending, update, last_flush_error) {

  payload <- isolate(pending())

  if (!has_any_changes(payload)) {
    reset_pending(pending)
    return(invisible(FALSE))
  }

  tryCatch(
    {
      update(payload)
      last_flush_error(NULL)
    },
    error = function(e) {
      last_flush_error(conditionMessage(e))
      log_warn(
        "flush_pending: dispatch rejected payload: ",
        conditionMessage(e)
      )
    },
    finally = reset_pending(pending)
  )

  invisible(TRUE)
}
```

The only change is the third arg and the two reactiveVal writes:
clear on success, populate on rejection. Phase 3's atomicity contract
is unchanged.

## Documentation deliverables

### Top-level tutorial vignette — `vignettes/blockr.assistant.Rmd`

Lives at the package root (not under `vignettes/design/`) so
`browseVignettes("blockr.assistant")` and pkgdown's "Get started"
slot pick it up. The design-doc vignettes stay under
`vignettes/design/` as articles, accessed via the pkgdown navbar.

Outline (one Rmd, ~250 lines):

1. *What this is.* Two sentences plus a screenshot of a populated
   board with the assistant panel.
2. *Mount it on a board.* Copy-paste runnable example: a
   `dock_board` with three blocks, the assistant extension, served.
3. *Talk to it.* A worked dialogue showing the model answering "what
   blocks are on the board?" (now answered from the prompt summary,
   no tool call), then "describe the head block" (one tool call),
   then "add a scatter plot of sepal length vs sepal width" (three
   staged mutations, one flush).
4. *Configure the model.* How to point at a different provider via
   `blockr_option("chat_function", …)`. Pointer to ellmer for the
   provider matrix.
5. *Customise the persona.* The `persona` argument; when to override
   the full prompt via `prompt_composer`.
6. *Extend the read tools.* The `describe_block.<class>` and
   `describe_stack.<class>` S3 generics. One short example for a
   bespoke block class.
7. *Where to go next.* Pointers to the design vignettes for
   contributors, and the issue tracker for feature requests.

Code chunks are not evaluated (`eval = FALSE`) — the package can't
talk to a live model in CI without a key. Screenshots ship under
`man/figures/`.

### Example app — `inst/examples/05-polish/app.R`

A single showcase app that exercises the full surface end-to-end
against a populated board. The Phase 4 example
(`04-mutation-tools/`) already exercises the mutation tool surface
on a near-empty board; the Phase 5 example complements it with a
realistic starting board so the model has something to navigate
*to*, not just from.

Structure: a `dock_board` with five blocks (data, filter, head,
plot1, plot2), two stacks, and the assistant. Comments at the top
of the file list the manual scenarios to try ("ask what's on the
board without calling a tool", "ask the assistant to add a third
plot", "ask to rename a block and observe the immutability
nudge").

Existing examples stay in place — `01-shell/` and `02-read-tools/`
are useful for regression and for the corresponding design phases'
documentation. `04-mutation-tools/` covers the mutation surface on
a clean board. No example is deleted by Phase 5.

### README — `README.Rmd`

A near-rewrite. The current README pins the lifecycle at "Phase 1"
and says "the assistant has no tools to inspect or manipulate the
board yet"; both are no longer accurate. The Phase 5 README:

- Lifecycle badge stays `experimental` (the package is still
  pre-1.0 even though feature-complete for the initial roadmap).
- *What it is*: one paragraph naming `ellmer`, `shinychat`,
  `blockr.dock`.
- *Install*: unchanged.
- *Example*: a runnable snippet — same shape as the existing one,
  but the screenshot is from the Phase 5 example app (assistant
  visible, populated board, one chat exchange visible in the
  panel).
- *What the assistant can do*: bullet list — read tools, mutation
  tools, dynamic board summary, conversation persistence
  (round-trips via ser/des, wiring is your call).
- *Roadmap link*: points at the roadmap article. Removes the
  per-phase progress noise that's now stale.
- *Design notes link*: points at the articles index for the
  per-phase docs.

### pkgdown — `_pkgdown.yml`

Two changes:

1. *Articles navbar*: a "Get started" entry pointing at
   `vignettes/blockr.assistant.Rmd`, and a "Design notes" section
   that surfaces the six design vignettes in roadmap order.
2. *Reference index*: grouped into "Extension" (`new_assistant_extension`,
   `default_persona`), "S3 generics" (`describe_block`,

   miscellany for anything that does not fit (currently empty —

The pkgdown site is already deployed via the existing CI workflow;
no infra changes.

## Acceptance criteria

### Automated (CI / `devtools::check()`)

- `compose_system_prompt()` against a fixture board emits the four
  sections in the documented order, with the headers
  (`## Tools`, `## Board`) present and the delta note absent when
  `last_flush_error()` is `NULL`.
- `format_tool_catalogue()` against a chat with the full Phase 2 +
  Phase 4 tool set emits one line per tool in registration order,
  with optional args marked `?` and required args bare.
- `summarise_board()` against:
  - An empty board → header + "(empty board — no blocks yet)".
  - A small populated board → header + per-block / per-link /
    per-stack lines.
  - A pathologically large board (1000 synthetic blocks) →
    header + "(too many blocks to inline; call list_blocks…)"
    truncation branch.
- Flush-rejection round-trip via `shiny::testServer()`:
  - Stage a payload that would invalidate against a mocked
    validator. Trigger `last_turn`. Assert `last_flush_error()`
    holds the rejection message.
  - Trigger `last_input` for the next turn. Assert the composed
    prompt contains `"Note: your previous turn's changes were
    rejected"`.
  - Trigger `last_turn` after a no-op turn. Assert
    `last_flush_error()` is `NULL` and the composed prompt no
    longer carries the note.
- Persona rename: passing `persona = "<custom>"` to
  `new_assistant_extension` sets the persona section of the
  composed prompt; passing nothing falls back to
  `default_persona()`.
- Prompt-composer escape hatch: passing `prompt_composer = function(persona, …) "X"`
  produces a system prompt of exactly `"X"`.
- The `state` round-trip: serialising an extension, restoring it,
  and reading the restored `state$persona` matches the original.
- Phase 1-4 acceptance criteria continue to pass.
- `devtools::check()` passes 0/0/0.
- `lintr::lint_package()` passes 0 lints.

### Manual (demo app, live LLM)

Run the Phase 5 example app against a real provider and verify:

- *Trivial question without a tool call.* "How many blocks are on
  the board?" Expected: the model answers from the prompt summary
  without invoking `list_blocks`. Inspect ellmer's turn record to
  confirm no tool call fired.
- *Drill-down with a tool call.* "Show me the current value of
  `n_rows` on the head block." Expected: one `describe_block`
  call, accurate answer.
- *Pipeline build.* "Add a filter for `Sepal.Width > 3` after the
  head block and pipe the result into a new scatter plot."
  Expected: the model stages the appropriate blocks and links in
  one turn; the flush succeeds; the new blocks appear on the
  board.
- *Rename request.* "Rename `head` to `top_rows`." Expected: the
  model declines the in-place rename, explains the `remove + add`
  path with the eval-state caveat, and asks the user. (Triggered
  by the persona's id-immutability paragraph; no tool call
  required.)
- *Recover from a flush rejection.* Set up a board where a staged
  link would create a cycle (manual setup via the example app's
  comments). Ask the assistant to add the cycle-creating link.
  Expected: the model reports staging success per tool call, then
  the flush rejects; on the next user prompt ("try again
  differently"), the model sees the delta note in its prompt and
  proposes a non-cyclic alternative without the user having to
  paste the error.

Manual checks are documentation, not gating — they verify the
prompt-context layer holds up in a real assistant loop and are
recorded in the PR description.

## Known limitations carried into later phases

- **Refresh only at user-turn boundaries.** UI-driven board edits
  that happen between turns are reflected on the next turn (because
  the prompt re-renders), but mid-turn UI edits are not visible to
  the model until *its next* turn. Same staleness window as the
  read tools; no regression.
- **No diff against last turn's summary.** "Block X's `n_rows`
  changed since you last looked" would help the model spot user
  edits, but introduces stateful comparison bookkeeping. The
  flush-rejection note is the only delta we ship; richer diffs
  wait on demand.
- **Tool catalogue is bag-of-tools, not categorised.** The
  catalogue lists every registered tool in registration order. For
  the current 15-tool surface this is readable; if per-block-type
  custom tools (#12) ever land, grouping by namespace might
  matter.
- **Persona override is all-or-nothing.** Callers who want to
  *add* to the default persona (not replace it) currently have to
  paste the default text into their override. A `persona = list(default = TRUE, append = "…")`
  variant is possible but adds surface; YAGNI for the initial
  roadmap.
- **No prompt-cache awareness.** The composer assembles sections
  in a stable order so providers that cache on prefix bytes (e.g.
  Anthropic's prompt caching) get decent hit rates, but we don't
  surface explicit cache breakpoint hints. ellmer may grow this
  API; we wire it up if/when it appears.
- **`list_pending_changes()` deferred.** Phase 4 left the door open
  for an explicit "show me what's staged" tool if empirical use
  showed the model getting confused. Phase 5's compact board
  summary covers the read side of the same friction; we'll
  observe and add the tool only if real users hit it.
- **No conversation persistence wiring.** Inherited from Phase 1.
  The `state$persona` and `state$messages` round-trip via
  `blockr.dock`'s ser/des, but cross-session save/restore (e.g.
  via `blockr.session`) is still application-level integration.
- **No snapshot / undo.** Inherited from the roadmap.
- **No inline tool-call approval UI.** Inherited from Phase 4.
  Mutation tools dispatch via staging at turn end; a "review
  before apply" gate is a future affordance.
